$comment: The lobby: what a guest can see in the weeks before the party. Presentation and costume only, never plot, which is why it is plaintext beside the encoded bible. A beat writes a character as {{C3}} and the name is substituted when it is served, so no character name is ever written down here.

copy.title: Before the night
copy.standfirst: You are cast. Here is who the room thinks you are, and what to wear. The dress code is come as you were: your character in 1989, not your character now. Everything private to you opens when the doors do.
copy.doorsNote: Your dossier, your secret and everything you are carrying into that room unlock at 7:00 on the night. Not before, not for anyone.

beats.title: Name tags are happening
beats.body: Every name tag is being written out by hand, in the handwriting of somebody who took pride in it in 1989 and has not improved since. If your name has an unusual spelling, this is the week to say so. It will not be corrected on the night. It will be laminated.

beats.title: Parking, and the one rule about it
beats.body: There is parking on the street and more of it behind the building. The one rule is that nobody blocks the side door, because the side door is how the food comes in and how anybody who needs a minute gets a minute. Carpool if you can. The hotel by the interstate runs a shuttle it does not advertise.

beats.title: The hall is booked. Actually booked.
beats.body: Third time asking. {{C1}} has the receipt, laminated, and has offered to show it to anyone who doubts it. The banner has been located. It has been in a box since 1991 and it smells like a box that has been closed since 1991. It is going up anyway. There are rooms held at the hotel by the interstate for anyone flying in, which is most of you.

beats.title: On the subject of the food
beats.body: The menu is settled and it is deliberately the food of the year: little sandwiches cut on the diagonal, a cheese ball, something in a slow cooker, and a vegetable tray nobody will finish. There will be a cake. There is a disagreement about the cake. The disagreement is ongoing.

beats.title: On the subject of the music
beats.body: There has been a disagreement about the playlist. One faction wants the year only. The other faction has pointed out that we graduated in June and the good songs came out in the autumn. A compromise has not been reached. Bring requests; bring stamina.

beats.title: Roll call
beats.body: The count says we are close to a full room. If you have said you are coming and have not picked up your character yet, this is the week. If you are still deciding, decide: the hall is booked either way and your name tag is already written.

beats.title: Somebody found the yearbooks
beats.body: Two of them, plus the one with the page torn out that everybody remembers and nobody will admit to. They are coming. So is a slide projector that may or may not work. If you have photographs, bring photographs. People are going to want to look at each other at seventeen before they look at each other now.

beats.title: About the slideshow
beats.body: There will be a slide show. Twelve slides, projected, put together from whatever was in the boxes. Nobody on the committee will say what is on all twelve. One of them has caused an argument already. Bring your own photographs anyway, because the memory table is going to need filling.

beats.title: Tomorrow
beats.body: Doors at seven, and it starts at seven, so seven-thirty means walking in during your own introduction. Charge your phone; it is the only thing you have to bring and it holds everything that is yours. Wear the year. Eat something first, then eat again when you get here.

C1.attire: Committee chair in a blouse with a real collar, a cardigan she will take off and put back on all night, dark trousers or a skirt, and flat shoes, with a lanyard she made herself. Going further, 1989 it properly: a pastel cardigan over a blouse with a bow at the throat, a permed bob with volume at the sides, pearl studs, and a clipboard she never once puts down. The look is somebody who has been ready since four o'clock.

C2.attire: The one who came dressed for a photograph: a blazer over a shell top, dark trousers or a pencil skirt, and shoes that cost something. Going further, put the shoulder pads back in the blazer, add big gold hoops, a heavy gold watch and a slick of red lipstick, and carry a leather folio nobody can explain. Dressed one notch above the room, entirely on purpose.

C3.attire: The one this room still goes quiet for when he picks up a microphone, dressed the way he dressed to give the senior speech: a jacket with some structure to it, a shirt, a wide patterned tie, and shoes that have been resoled twice. Going further, take 1989 all the way: a corduroy or tweed jacket, oversized wire-rimmed glasses, a knitted vest underneath, and a folded index card in the breast pocket he will produce at exactly the right moment. The clothes should say it before he does.

C4.attire: Off duty but never quite off: a crisp button-down or polo tucked in, dark jeans, a good belt and boots. Going further, take it to 1989: a varsity jacket over the shirt, aviators hooked in the collar, hair with some height, and a campaign button pinned somewhere she can pretend she forgot about. Neat and pressed beats fancy for this one.

C5.attire: Yearbook staff black, then and now: dark jeans or trousers, a black shirt or roll-neck, flat shoes she can crouch in, and a real camera on a strap if you can borrow one. Going further, add a canvas vest with too many pockets, slim eighties wire-frame glasses, a lens cap she holds all evening, and one roll of film in a pocket. Practical, unfussy, and standing slightly apart from the party.

C6.attire: The letter jacket. That is the whole costume and he is going to wear it. Under it, a plain tee or a polo, jeans and sneakers. Going further, make it high school: the jacket with every patch, a tee from a tournament nobody else remembers, white high-tops, and a class ring he will show you. The joke works because it still fits, mostly.

C7.attire: Sharp and unapproachable: a dark blazer, a good shirt, tailored trousers, and heels she can cross a room in. Going further, 1989 her: shoulders in the blazer, hair blown out big, a long coat she keeps on far longer than the room is cold, and one piece of jewelry that is clearly the expensive thing. Dressed like somebody who did not come here to be comfortable.

C8.attire: Treasurer forever: a button-down, a sweater over the top, chinos, and the kind of shoes you can stand in all night. Going further, go full 1989 bookkeeper: a sweater vest over a striped shirt, a calculator watch, glasses that slide down, and pens in the breast pocket. Fussy, kind, and slightly overdressed for a rented hall.

C9.attire: Cheer captain grown up and hosting: a good blouse with the sleeves pushed up, dark trousers, and shoes she can stand in for four hours. Going further, put 1989 back on: a bold blazer with the shoulders still in it, plenty of gold, hair that clearly took effort, and the old cheer letter pinned on as a joke that is not entirely a joke. Being slightly too dressed up for a rented hall is exactly right here.

C10.attire: Came straight off a shift and still outshines the room: a simple dress, or a silk shirt and trousers, comfortable shoes, and a phone that will not stop buzzing. Going further, bring out the 1989 homecoming tiara that has been in a drawer for thirty-five years, throw a shoulder-padded jacket over the top, and push reading glasses into your hair. Tidy, tired, and quietly the best-dressed person in the building by nine o'clock.

F1.attire: Comfortable and unbothered by the dress code: a bright top, jeans, clean sneakers, and a tote bag with something in it for you. Going further, take it to 1989 with a tracksuit jacket in a color you can see from the parking lot, a scrunchie, a fanny pack, and a visor. The look is somebody who is on her feet all day and dressed for it.

F2.attire: Only here for a year and a half, and she has decided to make up for the whole of it in one evening: whatever the internet told her 1989 looked like, worn with total confidence and no reference point at all. Going further, more of it: neon, a side ponytail, plastic bangles to the elbow, the lot. She graduated with this class knowing nine people, and she is having a better night than anybody who knew everyone.

F3.attire: Dressed for a curtain call: something with movement, something with a color, and a coat worn like a cape. Going further, full 1989 theater department: a dramatic scarf, a velvet blazer, rings on both hands, and hair with real architecture. He was left off the list on purpose, he is wildly overdressed, and both of those are the point.

F4.attire: Working, not attending: catering blacks, an apron, and shoes for a double shift. No costume, no period, nothing from 1989, which in a room full of people in shoulder pads is its own kind of funny. Graduated with this class and is spending the reunion carrying trays at it, entirely on purpose.

F5.attire: The valedictorian, still dressed not to be noticed: a plain button-down or a soft sweater, khakis or dark slacks, and sensible shoes. Going further, 1989 it: a shirt buttoned to the collar under a beige cardigan, a neat side part, tortoiseshell glasses, and a slim briefcase held with both hands. Somebody who dressed carefully in the hope of being left alone.

F6.attire: Crew, and proud of it: a black tee, jeans, boots, and a multi-tool on the belt. Going further, make it the AV kid at forty-five: a band tee from a tour in 1989, a flannel tied at the waist, a lanyard of laminates from every show since, and drumsticks in a back pocket. The one person in the room who is technically working and having the most fun.

F7.attire: Comfortable, warm and ready for anybody's crisis: a soft top, jeans or scrubs bottoms, and shoes built for twelve hours. Going further, 1989 diner counter: a pastel waitress-style shirt, a name badge, hair up with a scrunchie, and a pen behind the ear she genuinely forgets about. Dressed like the person everyone ends up telling things to.

F8.attire: Comfortable and going nowhere: a polo in the school colors or a zip jacket with a crest on it, pressed slacks, and white sneakers. Going further, go 1989 team manager: a stopwatch on a cord, a school cap, a roll of tape in a pocket, and a folded program he keeps checking. He picked a chair at half past seven and the room comes to him, which the clothes should say before he does.

F9.attire: Easy and unbothered: a soft sweater or a pretty blouse, neat jeans, and comfortable shoes. Going further, try a pastel eighties sweater with a collar popped underneath, hair with period volume, a banana clip, and a wallet of photographs that opens out like an accordion. Somebody who dressed for a pleasant evening rather than for an audience.

F10.attire: Here to work and dressed for the year anyway: a blazer with the shoulders still in it over a plain shirt, dark jeans or slacks, and a notebook that never goes away. Going further, commit to 1989 properly and then ruin it slightly by holding a phone up more than is polite. In costume like everybody else, the only person taking notes, and increasingly not writing the story he came for.
